security_audit.summary: The static command findings are mostly markdown false positives from inline paths, fenced examples, and slash command documentation. The only confirmed risks are the documented external MCP setup command and hardcoded ClickUp MCP URL, which require user consent and endpoint verification but do not show malicious intent.

remediation.issue: External MCP server setup is documented without an explicit trust warning.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to verify the ClickUp MCP endpoint and review requested OAuth permissions before adding or authenticating the server.

remediation.issue: The setup command uses a remote HTTP transport endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Document what data may be sent to ClickUp during sync and recommend least-privilege workspace access.

content.value_statement: Roadmap updates often drift between local planning files and ClickUp workspaces. This skill guides MCP-based setup, mapping, sync commands, and conflict rules.
actual_capabilities: Explains how local epics and milestones map to ClickUp tasks and subtasks.
Guides setup of the ClickUp MCP connection and OAuth authentication flow.
Documents commands for push, pull, sync, status, link, and unlink workflows.
Describes the local ClickUp configuration file and sync mapping fields.
Recommends conflict rules for status, points, and title changes.
limitations: Requires a configured ClickUp MCP server and valid OAuth authentication.
Does not include implementation code for the slash commands themselves.
Assumes a specific local roadmap structure with epics and milestones.
Conflict handling rules are simple and may not fit every team process.

use_cases.title: Connect a roadmap to ClickUp
use_cases.description: Set up the ClickUp MCP connection and map local planning items to workspace tasks.

use_cases.title: Keep engineering plans aligned
use_cases.description: Use pull, push, and sync workflows to reduce drift between local files and ClickUp status.

use_cases.title: Review sync conflicts safely
use_cases.description: Apply documented precedence rules before updating titles, points, or status values.

prompt_templates.title: Set up ClickUp sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure ClickUp synchronization for my local roadmap. Explain each setup step and what information I need.

prompt_templates.title: Map roadmap items
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me map my local epics and milestones to ClickUp tasks and subtasks. Show how the configuration should be organized.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned roadmap changes and tell me which ClickUp sync command to use. Include a dry-run checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve sync conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me resolve conflicts between local roadmap data and ClickUp. Apply the status, points, and title precedence rules.

output_examples.input: I need to connect my roadmap to ClickUp for the first time.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline MCP setup, OAuth authentication, workspace selection, and the local configuration values to confirm.

output_examples.input: My local milestone title differs from ClickUp. Which value wins?
output_examples.output: The skill would apply the documented conflict rule: local titles win because they represent planning intent.

output_examples.input: Before I push changes, what should I check?
output: Check sync status for unresolved links or conflicts.

best_practices: Pull from ClickUp before pushing local roadmap changes.
Use dry-run previews before any sync that changes remote tasks.
Verify OAuth permissions and workspace scope before connecting the MCP server.
anti_patterns: Do not push local changes before checking for remote updates.
Do not reuse sync mappings across unrelated ClickUp workspaces.
Do not authenticate the MCP server without reviewing the requested permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill synchronize?
faq.answer: It focuses on syncing local roadmap epics and milestones with ClickUp tasks and subtasks.

faq.question: Does it require ClickUp access?
faq.answer: Yes. Users need a ClickUp workspace and OAuth authentication through the ClickUp MCP server.

faq.question: Can it perform bidirectional sync?
faq.answer: The skill documents a bidirectional sync command and recommends pulling before pushing changes.

faq.question: How are conflicts handled?
faq.answer: The documented rules prefer ClickUp for status and local roadmap data for points and titles.

faq.question: Does it store credentials?
faq.answer: The visible skill text shows a local mapping configuration, but OAuth authentication is handled through MCP.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility, with setup guidance using Claude MCP commands.
